title: 21. Policy-as-Code (Kyverno & CEL Admission)
summary: Master declarative Kubernetes policy enforcement using Kyverno ClusterPolicy, Mutating/Validating admission webhooks, and native Kubernetes ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with CEL.
prerequisites: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards (Privileged, Baseline, Restricted)
YAML syntax and JSON schema validation
learningObjectives: Deploy Kyverno ClusterPolicy resources to validate, mutate, and generate Kubernetes objects
Enforce non-root execution, read-only root filesystems, and approved container registries
Write and test native Kubernetes ValidatingAdmissionPolicy resources using Common Expression Language (CEL)
Audit existing cluster workloads for compliance violations using the Kyverno CLI

curriculumModules.title: Kyverno: Kubernetes-Native Policy Engine
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kyverno policies are written as plain Kubernetes YAML without requiring proprietary languages (like Rego). Kyverno intercepts admission requests, validates specs against security baselines, and generates default objects.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Cluster-wide admission controller enforcing CIS benchmarks, image provenance, and team resource quotas.

curriculumModules.title: In-Tree ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with Common Expression Language (CEL)
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kubernetes 1.30+ features in-tree CEL admission control, executing declarative validation directly within the kube-apiserver binary without webhooks or network hops.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Ultra-low-latency in-tree CEL policies evaluating replica limits and mandatory team ownership labels.

labs.title: Kyverno ClusterPolicy for Disallowing Root Containers
labs.scenario: Your CISO mandated that no container in the production namespace may run as root (UID 0). Deploy a Kyverno ClusterPolicy named disallow-root-user that enforces runAsNonRoot: true.
labs.productionContext: Running containers as root is the #1 vector for container breakout exploits. Enforcing non-root admission blocks misconfigured pods before scheduling.
objectives: Deploy the disallow-root-user Kyverno ClusterPolicy in Enforce mode
Verify policy application using the Kyverno test command
Record verification proof in policy-audit ConfigMap
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: disallow-root-user
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: check-runasnonroot
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
              namespaces:
                - production
      validate:
        message: "Containers must have runAsNonRoot: true"
        pattern:
          spec:
            securityContext:
              runAsNonRoot: true
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: policy-audit
  namespace: production
data:
  policyName: "disallow-root-user"
  status: "active"

steps.title: Inspect Kyverno ClusterPolicy
steps.instruction: Open the Manifest Editor and review the disallow-root-user ClusterPolicy manifest.

steps.title: Deploy Policy and Audit Record
steps.instruction: Apply the ClusterPolicy and policy-audit ConfigMap to the cluster.

steps.title: Execute Policy Test
steps.instruction: Run kyverno apply to test the policy against sample workloads.

validationRules.description: ClusterPolicy disallow-root-user exists with validationFailureAction Enforce
validationRules.name: disallow-root-user
validationRules.remediation: Deploy ClusterPolicy disallow-root-user with spec.validationFailureAction: Enforce.

validationRules.description: ConfigMap policy-audit exists in production with status active
validationRules.name: policy-audit
validationRules.remediation: Apply the starter manifest to create the policy-audit ConfigMap.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure validationFailureAction is set to 'Enforce' rather than 'Audit'.

labs.title: Native ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with CEL Expressions
labs.scenario: To avoid external webhook latency, use Kubernetes native ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with Common Expression Language (CEL) to require all Deployments to have at least 2 replicas.
labs.productionContext: CEL-based ValidatingAdmissionPolicy eliminates admission webhook failure modes (e.g. timeout on apiserver when webhook pod is down).
objectives: Bind policy to production namespace with ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: check-min-replicas
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["deployments"]
  validations:
    - expression: "object.spec.replicas >= 2"
      message: "Deployments in production must have at least 2 replicas for high availability."
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: check-min-replicas-binding
spec:
  policyName: check-min-replicas
  validationActions: [Deny]
  matchResources:
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        environment: production

steps.title: Review CEL ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
steps.instruction: Inspect the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy manifest and its CEL expression.

steps.title: Apply CEL Policy and Binding
steps.instruction: Deploy the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and its binding to the cluster.

validationRules.description: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy check-min-replicas exists with failurePolicy Fail
validationRules.name: check-min-replicas
validationRules.remediation: Apply ValidatingAdmissionPolicy check-min-replicas with spec.failurePolicy: Fail.

validationRules.name: check-min-replicas-binding
validationRules.remediation: Apply the starter manifest to create ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Confirm the CEL expression syntax matches 'object.spec.replicas >= 2'.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary advantage of Kubernetes ValidatingAdmissionPolicy over traditional admission webhooks?
options: It runs in the apiserver using CEL without external network latency or webhook dependencies
It can run without a kube-apiserver
It only works on Windows nodes
It requires a separate etcd cluster
assessmentQuestions.explanation: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy executes Common Expression Language (CEL) directly within the kube-apiserver process, eliminating webhook timeouts.

assessmentQuestions.question: In Kyverno, which validationFailureAction setting rejects non-compliant resources at admission time?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: validationFailureAction: Enforce causes Kyverno to actively block and reject the admission request.
